MINUTES

  REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING

  DECEMBER 5, 2016

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:01 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Scott, Medawar, Chair Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang, Carman

Commissioners Absent:  Thomas

Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom, Planning
  Technician and Code Administrator Slawson

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO,

  TO APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF NOVEMBER 7, 2016.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

None.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  WAIVE READING IN FULL ALL RESOLUTION THAT ARE PRESENTED
  FOR THE PLANNING COMMISSION CONSIDERATION ON TONIGHT’S
  AGENDA AND ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE
  ONLY.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 6-A.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

--THE FOLLOWING ITEM WAS HEARD OUT OF ORDER AS A BUSINESS ITEM--

B.  BI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT REPORT.

Planning Director Wahba explained that this report was in a new format that would make it
more user-friendly, and it presented a quick snapshot of the cases that take a little bit more
time to resolve. Planning Director Wahba stated if the Commission had any questions about
these cases or any other that now was the time to ask.

Planning Commission Minutes  1
December 5, 2016
 In response to a question from CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER, Planning Technician and Code
Administrator Slawson explained that we have an exclusive contract with Waste Management,
and any dumpster or large roll-off waste bins used during construction must be obtained from
them.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba and
Planning Technician and Code Administrator Slawson explained that there is a handout at the
counter at City Hall as well as one at Building and Safety that details these dumpster
requirements, and that the information is also included in some of the newsletters.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER asked about the case involving feeding of wildlife at 901 Silver Spur,
to which Planning Technician and Code Administrator Slawson replied that behind the Town
and Country Shopping Center there is feeding of cats and that sometime the food is left out,
which encourages the coyotes so they have tried to track down the person who is feeding and
they routinely check the area out.

In response to questions from COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Technician and Code
Administrator Slawson stated that unpermitted construction was taking place too close to the
property line on Dapplegray Lane and a Stop Work Order was issued.

In regards to the short term rental on Sweetgrass, Planning Director Wahba stated that the
Short Term Rental Ordinance was adopted by City Council and was currently in effect, so they
have been working with some of the major on-line companies in regards to complaints that they
have received. Planning Technician and Code Administrator Slawson said that a courtesy letter
was sent to the homeowners on Sweetgrass which explained the new ordinance that had
passed and asked them to please take the listing off of the internet.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 6-B, THE BI-ANNUAL CODE ENFORCEMENT
  REPORT.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 30-16; APPLICANT: Mr. & Mrs. Matt McGovern;
  LOCATION: 1 Lazy Creek Lane; A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination to
  construct one- and two-story additions to a two-story home. Minor Deviations are
  required to: 1) decrease the front yard area by less than 10%; and 2) for encroachment
  of the additions into the required front yard which does not project closer to the property
  line than the forwardmost building line.

Associate Planner Thom summarized the Staff Report (as per written material) and stated that
she could answer any questions.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if there were any comments from neighbors, to which
Associate Planner Thom replied that there were not.

Russ Barto, Architect, stated that he was there to answer any questions from the Commission.

There being no questions, COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER
MEDAWAR to,

  TO APPROVE PA-30-16.

AYES:  Scott, Medawar, Yoo, Zigrang, Carman, Chair Schachter,
NOES:
ABSTAIN:
ABSENT:  Thomas

Planning Director Wahba explained the 20-day appeal period for Item 7-A.

Planning Commission Minutes  2
December 5, 2016
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-16; APPLICANT: Ms. Judy Chai; LOCATION: 5338
  Crest Road. A request for a General Plan Amendment, Zone Change (from
  Commercial-Limited to RA-10 Residential), Tentative Parcel Map, Grading Application
  and Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for the construction of two single-family
  patio homes on a .51-acre parcel. A Mitigated Negative Declaration is also requested
  under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). (KT)

Associate Planner Thom summarized the Staff Report (as per written material).

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER YOO, Planning Director Wahba stated that
the silhouette had only been up for one week instead of the required two. The silhouette that
was up was only capturing the main ridge line because if there was going to be any view
impairment it would be from those ridges. He added that it was difficult to tell without actually
getting inside the units, but that units #49 and #51 Seaview Drive South may be affected but he
said he guessed that there was probably not a view impairment given that it had gone up only a
few feet. He added that they had not heard from either of those units that would be most
impacted. Planning Director Wahba further explained that #51 had let the hedge at their side of
the property run up, whereas #49 has kept their hedges topped.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked whether the view would be impaired if the hedges were
trimmed at #51, and Planning Director Wahba answered that, in general, views are considered
to be from the primary living areas of homes, including the master bedroom, but that these
windows didn’t appear to be from those areas of the home.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT noted that the southernmost unit in #51 is a vacant unit, to which
Planning Director Wahba stated that #49 appeared vacant as well.

In response to a question from CHAIRMAN SCHAHCTER, Planning Director Wahba stated that
the staking would be kept up for the City Council meeting, but that he wanted any possible view
impairments to be addressed before the case went to Council.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered.

Gary Maxwell (Architect, Maxwell & Associates, Huntington Beach) stated that due to design
constraints of the single driveway the pad had to be brought up in height. He said that for the
home closest to the adjacent properties, the maximum ridge line was 16’ long, and the ridge
was 33’ long on the house closer to Crest Road.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT said that though he understood why they had to lift the pads, he felt
it was unfortunate that there was more pavement on the property than before. He added that
he was surprised that the back house view was blocked by the front home, because he thought
the views would be staggered. Mr. Maxwell said that they pushed the second stories so they
looked past each other, and that the view was not directly onto Crest but to the side.

Helen Cannefax, (22 Seaview Drive North, President of Seaview Villas Homeowners
Association) came forward. She stated that this was an important consideration not just for the
two units that were referenced but also for all of Seaview’s residents. She added that the
Association had received no notification of the hearings and wouldn’t have known if they weren’t
in such close contact with Ms. Chai. She had received a copy of the mailing list and felt that
some of the units that should have been notified weren’t, and that some of the units on the list
said “Seaview Drive South” when they were “Seaview Drive North.” She added that she didn’t
know if some of the absentee owners received notices either, and that some of the properties
had been sold and they didn’t know if the new owners received notices in the interim.

Planning Director Wahba clarified for the Commission how mailing lists are created using
information from the County Tax Assessor’s office, which is updated on a quarterly basis. He
suggested that staff bring this project back later, perhaps to the Adjourned meeting of January

Planning Commission Minutes  3
December 5, 2016
 9, 2017, after renotifying the public hearing to make sure everyone has seen the plans.

Ms. Cannefax returned to the dais and suggested that the homeowners could discuss the
project at their annual HOA meeting on December 14th, which has the largest turn-out of the
year.

Tom Alley, (6304 Sattes, Rancho Palos Verdes) came forward and stated that although he lives
in Rancho Palos Verdes he owns a home in 17 Seaview Drive South on the south side. He
said the longer row of staking flags closer to Crest Road showed a view impairment. He added
that he went out there with his 25’ tape and tried to measure from the ground up to the top of
that flag and the best he could estimate was 26’, when in fact he hears that the roof was 22’.
He asked how much the ground was being raised. In response to a question from
COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba stated that the grade was being raised 3’,
whereupon COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked that the Architect return to the dais.

Mr. Maxwell, returned to the dais. COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked whether the raising of the
pad would cause it to be a few feet above the sidewalk, and CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER asked
why they needed the 3’ increase in elevation. Mr. Maxwell stated that after speaking with the
Civil Engineer, he was told that it was necessary in order to get proper drainage to the site.

COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that from a construction point-of-view he agreed that if the
elevation was left flat, there would be no drainage and it would pool water.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he didn’t understand why the pad would be raised 3’ from
where it is today. Planning Director Wahba clarified that with the patio homes they were
actually lowering the site. The net change from what is there today to what is proposed is only
going up about 1’18” so the net change from how the patio homes were silhouetted was about
3’ but the grade itself is only going up a foot.

Planning Director Wahba wondered if it was silhouetted incorrectly, and added that it was a 3’
change of silhouette height, not pad height. He said he would verify the silhouette with the
Engineer.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER stated that in light of the HOA concerns and the opposition and the
silhouette issues, that they should continue this to January 9, 2017, to resolve these issues.

Judy Chai, Applicant, came forward and asked for clarification on the directions that were to be
given by the Planning Commission, because it would be easier for her during her presentation
to the HOA if she could say that the City had no objection.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER stated that they were wanting to continue it to January 9, 2017,
whereupon it could possibly be approved at that time if the HOA does not object.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that if view impaction was an issue for the HOA at the time of
the next meeting, then they needed to submit pictures demonstrating such.

CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered that they will continue this matter until January 9, 2017,
for review by staff with the HOA.

Planning Director Wahba stated that they would renotify beyond the 500’ radius to make sure
everyone in the Seaview Drive (North and South) HOA was notified.

--THE FOLLOWING ITEM WAS HEARD OUT OF ORDER--

8-B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 33-16; APPLICANT: Mr. & Mrs. Morley Mendelson;
  LOCATION: 4 Silver Saddle Lane; A Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and a
  Variance to install a 50-panel, 4’ high ground-mounted solar array in the front yard.

Planning Director Wahba stated that due to the fact that further information is needed, staff
recommends that this project be continued to the Adjourned Planning Commission meeting of
January 9, 2017, and that this item will be re-published and noticed accordingly.

Planning Commission Minutes  4
December 5, 2016
 CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER so ordered that this item would be re-noticed and heard at the
Adjourned Planning Commission meeting of January 9, 2017.

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked Planning Director Wahba if he could take care of a problem
with multiple telephone poles on the utility right-of-way on Palos Verdes Drive North near
Montecillo Drive. Planning Director Wahba said that he would work with the Public Works
Director in regards to this issue.

10.  DIRECTOR'S ITEMS

Planning Director Wahba announced to the Planning Commission that Planning Secretary,
Hollis Jackson, was going to retire at the end of the month and that she would be missed very
much. The Commission thanked her for her hard work, and Planning Director Wahba gave her
flowers in appreciation.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES MINUTES (11/21/16).

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS (11/15/16).

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11.A AND B.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER SO ORDERED.

13.  ADJOURNMENT

At 8:09 p.m. CHAIRMAN SCHACHTER adjourned the Planning Commission meeting to an
Adjourned Planning Commission meeting on January 9, 2017, at 7:00 p.m.

Hollis Jackson  Douglas R. Prichard
Minutes Secretary  City Clerk

Planning Commission Minutes  5
